key_insight: An expert-guided causal AI model estimated early fluid and vasopressor dosing recommendations for septic shock using clinician knowledge to reduce confounding.
clinical_relevance: It may help ICU teams standardize early haemodynamic decisions while accounting for patient-specific physiology, but it is not yet proven to improve outcomes.
method: Built a graphical causal inference model from clinician expertise
Trained on 1,706 MIMIC ICU admissions and externally validated on 1,450 eICU admissions
Compared recommended vs deviated fluid and vasopressor doses over the first 6 hours
evidence_signal: External validation showed moderate discrimination for survival (AUROC 0.72) and clinical improvement (AUROC 0.70), with treatment-effect estimates varying by baseline physiology.
watch_item: Observed associations are confounded by indication and the recommendations need prospective testing before clinical use.
paper_title: The Causal Artificial Intelligence Clinician for early haemodynamic management of septic shock in ICU
